videos.title: The Quiet Mathematics of a Balanced Mobile #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: Asymmetrical sculpture immediately embodies resting balance. The opening is still and may be too restrained for some viewers.
editorial.mechanism: Opposing torque directions and equal products lead to a recursively balanced branch; the center-of-mass marker stays under the support.
editorial.readability: Numerals, lever braces and center-of-mass label stay separate in the inspected samples.
editorial.pacing: Measured 79 seconds; important equalities have visible holds, but speech remains almost continuous.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. Full decode and independent ASR differences reviewed. No subjective listening or claim of pleasing prosody.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The drawing remains a simplified diagram rather than a sensuous sculpture. An imbalance-and-recovery comparison would teach more directly than equal products alone.
editorial.audience_evidence: Not measured. No retention, recognition, learning or subscription results yet.

videos.title: How a Third Filter Lets Light Through #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: Adding a middle filter restores a nonzero meter, a concrete surprise without a hype claim.
editorial.mechanism: Two field projections lead to half and quarter intensities relative to light after the first filter; rotations reach zero at both outside axes.
editorial.readability: Rebuilt to separate the intensity formula from three-line captions; final samples show clear spacing.
editorial.pacing: 96 seconds gives each projection time, although the distinction between field and intensity remains demanding.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. Full decode and independent ASR differences reviewed. No subjective listening or claim of pleasing prosody.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The front-view filters and lower vector diagram still need mental integration. A single traveling field representation would connect them more directly. ASR transcribed Malus as malice; spelling alone does not establish wrong pronunciation.

videos.title: The Even Rhythm Inside an Uneven Orbit #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: The ellipse establishes an uneven orbital rhythm with the Sun at a focus.
editorial.mechanism: Equal-time sectors visibly have equal area; a local triangle, radial force and stated angular momentum relation connect to the ideal central-force model.
editorial.readability: The area colors, Sun, radius and labels remain distinct through sampled transitions; final sectors share the same focus.
editorial.pacing: 92 seconds; equal-area painting is the most satisfying payoff, while the angular momentum passage asks for more background knowledge.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. Full decode and independent ASR differences reviewed. No subjective listening or claim of pleasing prosody.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: A novice can follow equal areas more easily than the explanation of conserved angular momentum. The triangle-to-area-rate inference could be enlarged and separated into a quiet beat. The orbit is deliberately exaggerated and idealized.
editorial.audience_evidence: Not measured. No retention, recognition, learning or subscription results yet.
